title: Count Pairs of Equal Substrings With Minimum Difference
summary: Given two strings, count the number of index quadruples (i,j,a,b) where the substring from i to j in the first string matches the substring from a to b in the second string, and the difference between j and a is minimized among all matching substrings.
statement: Given two strings, count the number of index quadruples (i,j,a,b) where the substring from i to j in the first string matches the substring from a to b in the second string, and the difference between j and a is minimized among all matching substrings.
constraints: Count equal nonempty substring pairs whose value j-a is globally minimum.
Indices i,j belong to the first string and a,b to the second.
hints: Any longer equal substring contains a one-character equal pair with no larger j-a.
For each character, only its latest position in the second string can minimize the difference.
Scan first-string positions, compare index minus the stored latest matching index, and count ties.
Reducing every candidate to its ending character preserves or improves j-a; the latest second occurrence is optimal for that character, so the scan counts exactly all global minima.
editorial: Reducing every candidate to its ending character preserves or improves j-a; the latest second occurrence is optimal for that character, so the scan counts exactly all global minima.

tests.explanation: The single-character match a at first index zero and second index four uniquely minimizes j-a.
The strings share no character, so no equal substring pair exists.
